notesStmt.note: This proof slip, with notations and corrections in Whitman's hand, is dated "June 1885" at the top. One of Whitman's daybooks indicates that he first sent the poem to Harper's on June 7, 1885, but that it was rejected (see Walt Whitman, Daybooks and Notebooks, ed. William White, vol. 2, Daybooks, December 1881–1891 [New York University Press, 1978], 359). It was then accepted by Outing and published in August 1885. The corrections on this slip therefore likely date to May or early June 1885.

note.p: This is a corrected proof slip of the poem "The Voice of the Rain," which was first published in Outing: A Journal of Recreation in August 1885. It was later included in November Boughs (1888).

lg.head: A RAIN ENIGMAThe Voice of the Rain.
lg.l: And who art thou? said I to the soft-falling shower,
Which, strange to tell, gave me an answer, as here translated:
I am the Poem of Earth, said the ‸voice of the rain.

Eternal I rise,δ impalpablye/ out of the land and the bottomless
sea,

Upward to heaven, whence, vaugely form'd, altogether changed,
and yet the same.,/

I descend to lave the drouths, atomies, dust-layers of the
globe,
And all that ‸in them with out me were seeds only, latent, unborn,

And forever, by day and night, ‸I give back life to my own
origin, and make pure and beautify it:

‸(/For song, issuing from its birth-place, after fulfilment, wan-
deringwandering
,
Reck'd or unreck'd, duly with love returns.‸)/
